title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2611.21176v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential route to automating scientific programming, but their usefulness depends on consistently producing numerically correct code. We extend FEM-Bench to 17 finite element tasks involving nonlinear and history-dependent mechanics and structural dynamics, and evaluate 15 models on implementation and test generation without execution feedback. The best model succeeds in 87.1% of single-pass implementation trials, but rankings differ between tracks. The leading implementer achieves 49.9% joint test success, while the leading tester reaches 82.6%. For six models, we compare single-pass generation with two agentic harnesses that allow code execution and revision. Agentic execution solves some tasks that never succeeded in single-pass trials and improves consistency on others, but gains vary across models and harnesses, and regressions also occur. translated_title: 基于大语言模型的科学编程：来自有限元分析的证据
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）为自动化科学编程提供了一条潜在途径，但其实用性取决于能否持续生成数值正确的代码。我们将FEM-Bench扩展至17个涉及非线性和历史相关力学以及结构动力学的有限元任务，并在无执行反馈的条件下对15个模型的代码实现和测试生成能力进行了评估。表现最好的模型在单次实现试验中的成功率达到87.1%，但两个赛道的排名并不一致：最佳实现模型在联合测试中成功率为49.9%，而最佳测试生成模型达到82.6%。对于其中六个模型，我们比较了单次生成与两种允许代码执行和修订的智能体框架。智能体执行解决了一些在单次尝试中从未成功的任务，并提高了其他任务的稳定性，但收益因模型和框架而异，且也出现了性能回退的情况。Claude Opus 5结合SimpleAgent达到了96.5%的Pass@3。
tldr: 该论文将FEM-Bench扩展至17个涉及非线性力学与结构动力学的有限元编程任务，对15个大语言模型的评估表明，单次生成的正确率有限，而结合代码执行与修订的智能体框架能显著提升性能（最高达96.5% Pass@3），揭示了LLM在自动化科学编程中的潜力与局限。
en_tdlr: The paper extends FEM-Bench to 17 finite element tasks involving nonlinear mechanics and structural dynamics, and shows through evaluation of 15 LLMs that while single-pass generation has limited success, agentic execution frameworks allowing code execution and revision significantly boost performance (up to 96.5% Pass@3), revealing both the potential and limitations of LLMs in automating scientific programming.
